nodes.label: Call Graph Backend Spike
nodes.rationale: Settles the TS 6 vs TS 7 era question empirically on real repos (a 73-file Next.js app, a Redwood app, cal.com's 31 projects) rather than from documentation, because the capability matrix's paper reading of TS 7 turned out to be wrong.

nodes.label: Checker.getSignatureUsage
nodes.rationale: Returns {name, call?} per reference, resolving through barrel files and renamed re-exports, which a syntactic tool cannot reach. Chosen as the call-graph primitive over getReferencesToSymbolInFile because the latter is file-scoped and alias-blind (returns 0 for a call through an alias).

nodes.label: Call-Site Sweep Algorithm
nodes.rationale: Enumerate every call site client-side from the local AST and resolve callees in batches of 500 with getSymbolAtLocation. Chosen over per-symbol querying because it is 30x faster (4.1 s vs a projected 121.9 s on cal.com apps/web), produces a strict superset of the edges, needs no callable-classification heuristic (the call site tells you), and resolves method dispatch to the declared target instead of the union across all implementations.

nodes.label: Per-Symbol Call Query
nodes.rationale: Rejected: asking 'who calls X' per symbol scans the whole program each time (12.6 ms per call at 3,000 files, 98% of total time) and cannot be batched — passing an array throws 'getNodeId requires a RemoteNode'. Cost is O(callables x program size), projected 122 s for one cal.com project.

nodes.label: A JSX Element Is A Call
nodes.rationale: JSX invocations are reported with `call` undefined, so trusting `.call` alone drops 27% of a Next.js repo's call graph with no diagnostic. One client-side rule (opening or self-closing tag is an invocation; the closing tag is the same invocation) restores 150/150 parity with TS 6.

nodes.label: getSignatureUsage Wants The VariableDeclaration
nodes.rationale: For `const f = () => {}` the VariableDeclaration yields 2 usages while the ArrowFunction initialiser and the name Identifier both yield 0, with no error. Arrow consts are the dominant callable shape in modern TypeScript, so passing the wrong node produces an empty call graph and no indication anything is wrong.

nodes.label: NodeHandle.path Case Normalisation
nodes.rationale: NodeHandle.path is lowercased on macOS while Program.getSourceFileNames() preserves real casing, so ids built from each never match. It surfaced as an apparent 0-of-13 backend disagreement; path normalisation therefore belongs at the adapter boundary, once.

nodes.label: Method Dispatch Over-Approximation
nodes.rationale: getSignatureUsage returns every sibling implementation's call sites for each declaration, so PaypalGateway.capture is reported as called at a site constructing a StripeGateway. Method edges through a shared name are therefore inferred, not deterministic — a property of the type checker, identical in TS 6.

nodes.label: Dynamic Dispatch Is Invisible
nodes.rationale: gateway[methodName](n) produces no edge — correctly no false edge, but silently no real one either, so impact under-reports and codedocs cannot know it did.

nodes.label: Reachable-But-Callerless Code
nodes.rationale: Every Redwood Cell export (QUERY, Loading, Empty, Failure, Success) has zero call edges because the framework consumes them, so a naive 'no callers implies dead' rule deletes an app's whole data layer. Worse, the signal is inconsistent across sibling cells, so partial evidence reads like real evidence — any dead-code claim needs a framework-entry-point escape hatch and must degrade to 'unable to verify'.

nodes.label: Nearest-Named-Ancestor Caller Attribution
nodes.rationale: enclosingNamed walks out to the nearest named declaration, but module-level calls have none (so the model needs a File/Module node that can be a caller), 28 Redwood call sites inside anonymous it(...) callbacks are unattributed, and a call in a variable initialiser attributes to the variable (brokenCaller.result) rather than the function.

nodes.label: A Repository's Call Graph Is A Quarter Of Its Call Sites
nodes.rationale: On cal.com the sweep resolved 81,888 call sites into the repo's own symbol table and left 251,648 unattributed, overwhelmingly node_modules calls. Deduplicated the ratio moves only from 24.6% to 22.5%, so whatever trace and impact claim must be honest about the other three quarters.

nodes.label: Preflight Cost At Repository Scale
nodes.rationale: getSemanticDiagnostics over every cal.com file costs 36.4 s whole-repo — more than the call graph itself — so preflight cannot be an unconditional first phase; it must be incremental, scoped, or both.

nodes.label: TS 6 Cannot Open A Real Monorepo
nodes.rationale: In-process, cal.com's 31 projects exhaust an 8 GB heap after 66 s and abort during project open ('Ineffective mark-compacts near heap limit'); TS 7 completes the same work at 2.4 GB peak. TS 6 survives only process-per-project, at roughly half the speed everywhere.

nodes.label: Unprepared Repo Returns A Plausible Wrong Answer
nodes.rationale: Redwood measured before `yarn rw g types` returned a graph 5 edges and 131 symbols short — 30% short on symbols — with no error, no empty result and no warning. Also: 302 of cal.com's 542 unresolved specifiers are one missing generated artefact, and cal.com's own `prisma generate` remediation fails under Node 24, so a reported remediation may not work.

nodes.label: Provenance Is Per Edge Instance
nodes.rationale: A function call edge is deterministic while the same edge kind through a shared method name is inferred, so provenance cannot be a per-edge-type constant — the model must carry it per edge instance.

nodes.label: Capability Matrix
nodes.rationale: Scores every candidate tool against PRD §6/§7's required facts to answer whether 'no custom static-analysis engine' can be honoured, and by which combination.

nodes.label: RUN / SRC / DOC Evidence Tiers
nodes.rationale: Every claim is tagged by how it was verified — executed against a fixture, read from shipped type definitions or source, or read from vendor documentation — so that nothing rests on a blog post, a comparison article, or recollection, and unverifiable claims are labelled UNVERIFIED rather than asserted.

nodes.label: TypeScript 6.0 Language Service
nodes.rationale: The only candidate shipping LSP-level aggregates as callable functions (findReferences, call hierarchy, getImplementationAtPosition, getNavigationTree) and the API every editor tool already targets. Its cost is being the pre-native compiler on a sunset trajectory.

nodes.label: TypeScript 7 unstable/sync API
nodes.rationale: A Node client driving the bundled tsgo Go binary over a pipe; verified to resolve user.save() to UserRepository.save across files through an interface. Ships no navigation tree, no call hierarchy and no getImplementationAtPosition, and Microsoft states in writing that 7.0 'does not ship with an API' and that 7.1 will bring a new and different one.

nodes.label: tsgo LSP Surface
nodes.rationale: The same Go binary reached over LSP rather than the API pipe. Method strings for prepareCallHierarchy, references, implementation and documentSymbol are compiled into the binary, but string presence proves only protocol vocabulary, not handling — named the single highest-value unknown in the document.

nodes.label: ts-morph 28
nodes.rationale: Vendors its own TypeScript 6.0 compiler, so it is an ergonomics layer over candidate A rather than an independent producer; it cannot reach TS 7 performance and ties codedocs to a third party's compiler-upgrade cadence.

nodes.label: oxc-parser
nodes.rationale: Purely syntactic and per-file, but returns ESM import/export information directly and pairs with oxc-resolver to make import edges without a type checker. Its strongest endorsement of the layered design is that Oxc embedded typescript-go (oxlint-tsgolint) rather than writing a checker.

nodes.label: ast-grep
nodes.rationale: Its own FAQ states it supports no scope, type, control-flow or data-flow analysis, so it is a structural pattern matcher — excellent for pattern discovery and rule-driven labelling over an assembled graph, and the wrong tool for building the symbol graph.

nodes.label: tree-sitter Tags Queries
nodes.rationale: Tags are documented as single-file only, with no inter-file linking or type information. Its genuine differentiator, error-tolerant incremental parsing of a dirty buffer, is not something a CLI product needs in v1.

nodes.label: scip-typescript
nodes.rationale: CLI-only, on the pre-6 JS compiler API, and SCIP has no call edge, so calls must be derived from an occurrence inside an enclosing_range. Its strategic value is the symbol ID scheme, not the tool: adopt SCIP-shaped ids and the interchange format comes free.

nodes.label: Graphify As Analysis Candidate
nodes.rationale: Ruled off the deterministic path: its TS resolution is tree-sitter plus name heuristics, its highest-value call edges are explicitly the LLM's job, and its own graph.json is a concept graph over a corpus rather than a symbol graph over a program. It stays a sibling tool for documents and rationale.

nodes.label: Stack Graphs Ruled Out As Dead
nodes.rationale: Conceptually the perfect middle layer — incremental cross-file name binding with no build system — but the GitHub repo is archived and the TypeScript crate has not moved since 2024. Do not depend on it.

nodes.label: Nothing Produces A Whole-Program Call Graph
nodes.rationale: Every candidate that resolves a call correctly does so one symbol at a time, so codedocs must drive a per-symbol API across every symbol and assemble the result. That is the largest engineering item and where the performance risk lives; it must not be mistaken for 'an existing tool already does this'.

nodes.label: Symbol Identity Is Not Free
nodes.rationale: The TS 7 checker gives an import specifier a different symbol id from the declaration it aliases, and getReferencesToSymbolInFile found zero references in importing files, so alias-following via getAliasedSymbol is mandatory and a stable cross-file id scheme (SCIP being the obvious prior art) must be decided before implementation.

nodes.label: implements / extends Asymmetry
nodes.rationale: getBaseTypes returns the base class for `extends` but an empty array for `implements`, so implementation edges must be read from AST heritage clauses or recomputed from type assignability.

nodes.label: Layered Analysis Pipeline
nodes.rationale: A type layer for symbols, calls and inheritance; a cheap syntactic oxc sweep for imports, exports and the JS best-effort path; manifest readers for packages and workspace bounds; and git for change facts — all behind one adapter into the codedocs model, with ast-grep and graphify layered over the assembled model, never under it.

nodes.label: No-Custom-Engine Constrains Analysis, Not Aggregation
nodes.rationale: No required fact obliges codedocs to write a parser or type checker, but no surveyed tool emits a whole-repository symbol-and-relationship graph either. The driver, the normalised model and the store are the irreducible job, so the rule must be read as constraining the analysis rather than the assembly — stated in as many words so nobody mistakes the assembler for a violation.

nodes.label: Dependency Licence Audit
nodes.rationale: Every licence was read from a primary source (the project's own LICENSE file, or registry metadata) on a recorded date, because licences change — the audit found a live counter-example in Graphify.

nodes.label: Closed-Source Commercial Distribution Assumption
nodes.rationale: codedocs is a proprietary CLI sold as a one-time purchase, so the only question asked of each dependency is whether it may be redistributed inside a closed-source product for money with no obligation to open codedocs' own source.

nodes.label: Library Versus Subprocess Consumption
nodes.source_location: Does subprocess vs library change the answer?
nodes.rationale: Permission is identical either way, but obligations are not: MIT and Apache-2.0 notice duties trigger on distribution, so a user-installed subprocess costs nothing while bundling a binary is distribution in Object form with no 'separate process' exemption. Hence: prefer user-installed subprocesses for the heavy tools and bundle only the libraries genuinely needed in-process.

nodes.label: Graphify Relicensing Volatility
nodes.rationale: Marked AMBIGUOUS for governance, not for its current licence: a single-maintainer project that went MIT at 0.8.37 to Apache-2.0 at 0.9.53 and moved to a new GitHub org inside one 0.x series can relicense again, and the MIT to Apache to BSL/SSPL drift is a recognised pattern. Mitigations: subprocess-only (recommended), hard-pin and archive the wheel plus its licence files, or keep the seam abstract so a relicence is a swap.

nodes.label: psycopg LGPL Disqualification
nodes.rationale: The single copyleft hit in the whole transitive tree, reachable only through graphifyy[postgres]. LGPL-3.0's relinking and installation-information duties are painful for a bundled commercial CLI, so the postgres extra must never be enabled — enforced as a build-time check on the bundled dependency set.

nodes.label: Apache-2.0 NOTICE Reproduction Duty
nodes.rationale: Apache-2.0 §4(a)-(d) requires shipping the licence text, retained notices and the verbatim NOTICE contents, which for TypeScript also drags in the vendored vscode-jsonrpc MIT licence — and for Oxc the separate THIRD-PARTY-LICENSE covering ~15 upstream projects, plus one MIT notice per tree-sitter grammar.

nodes.label: THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES Artefact
nodes.rationale: Ship one notices file beside the binary and surface it from the CLI (`codedocs licences`): full text per distinct licence, per-package copyright lines including each grammar separately, verbatim NOTICE contents, Oxc's third-party file, and an explicit dual-licence election for Biome.

nodes.label: Licence Re-Verification And Allowlist Gate
nodes.rationale: Licences are not stable facts, so re-verify on every version bump from the adopted version's own metadata, record the SPDX id and licence-file SHA beside the pin so drift is detectable in CI, fail the build outside a permissive allowlist, and archive the licence files — grants are irrevocable for the copy received only if you can prove the terms on the day.

nodes.label: Edge Count Reconciliation
nodes.rationale: Reconciles the spike's 81,888 edges against the skeleton's 26,091 with no residue, so that the three ADRs quoting the old figure keep their verdicts and only correct their numbers.

nodes.label: Project-File Multiplicity
nodes.rationale: cal.com's 4,827 files produce 17,113 file-project pairs (3.545x) under the skeleton's 28 projects and 19,231 (3.984x) under the spike's 31; 59.5% of files belong to more than one project and one belongs to 18. Both discovery rules see exactly the same files, so the edge gap was never a membership gap.

nodes.label: Edges Counted Once Per Project
nodes.rationale: One line caused it: symbols() held its `seen` set outside the project loop while callEdges() declared it inside, so declarations were deduplicated and call sites were not. Collapsing on (from, to, file, pos) gives 23,039 — a 3.554x over-count tracking the 3.545x file multiplicity almost exactly.

nodes.label: Canonical Project Per File
nodes.rationale: Restricting the sweep to each file's canonical project costs exactly 2 edges out of 23,039, both an ambient declaration (business-days-plugin.d.ts) that only some projects include. Cheap enough to keep, and the loss is honest because the site is still stored with a cause.

nodes.label: File-Attributed Call Edges
nodes.rationale: The 3,054 call sites with no named enclosing declaration are discarded by the spike and become real edges attributed to the file in the skeleton — the whole remaining difference between 23,037 and 26,091.

nodes.label: Nearest Callable Ancestor Attribution
nodes.rationale: All 5,905 differing edges credit a strict ancestor of the node the spike credited, with zero unrelated cases: the spike stops at the nearest named ancestor and the skeleton at the nearest callable one, so a call in a variable initialiser reads loadConfig rather than loadConfig.env.

nodes.label: Symbol Ids Collapsing On Anonymous Scopes
nodes.rationale: 48,517 declarations collapse to 41,771 ids because an anonymous callback contributes no segment to a qualified name, so two `const schema` locals in sibling it(...) blocks are indistinguishable — worst case 69 declarations under one id. Bounded (6,690 of 6,746 are non-durable locals, mostly in tests) but a callers answer for such an id over-reports, so it is real imprecision.

nodes.label: Index Size Overshoot
nodes.rationale: The real index holds a third of the sized edge count and still measures 51.3 MB, so the overshoot is worse than believed. Interning ids attacks symbol and call_edge (66% of the file), but unresolved_call is 8.4 MB of repeated file paths and callee text that the original arithmetic never counted at all.

nodes.label: Incremental Re-Analysis Research
nodes.rationale: Establishes the minimum work to bring a type-aware symbol graph back to correctness after one changed file, measured rather than argued: 3-5 ms and 1-3 files against 535 ms cold.

nodes.label: Signature-Gated Invalidation Wave
nodes.rationale: Tell the compiler the file changed, re-extract that file, and propagate to direct importers only where the export-shape hash actually changed. The gate is the whole game: without it an edit at the base of the graph costs 1,435 files and 261 ms; with it, 1-3 files and 3 ms — a 107-178x saving.

nodes.label: Export-Shape Hash
nodes.rationale: Computed from typeToString, expanding Interface, TypeAlias, Class and Enum structurally via getDeclaredTypeOfSymbol plus getPropertiesOfType — never from Type.id, and never from getTypeOfSymbol alone.

nodes.label: .tsbuildinfo Format
nodes.rationale: Read for inspiration, never depend on it: undocumented, demonstrably changed between 6.0.3 and 7.0.2, discarded wholesale on any compiler version change, and only written by an emitting build a read-only tool has no reason to run. Its value is corroboration — referencedMap is the import graph and `signature` is the shape hash, exactly the two things the recommended algorithm needs.

nodes.label: Project References As An Analysis Boundary
nodes.rationale: Only partly reusable: a solution-style root tsconfig yields one project with zero files and is not expanded, so leaf configs must be enumerated; and `paths`-to-source — the dominant pnpm/Turborepo convention — makes one package pull in the whole workspace, so cheap partitioning cannot be assumed.

nodes.label: getDefaultProjectForFile
nodes.rationale: A file can appear in N projects and legitimately have N different sets of symbol facts (different strict, different lib), so codedocs must pick one canonical project per file and treat other projects' views as secondary.

nodes.label: Type Ids Are Not Stable
nodes.rationale: Type ids are assigned lazily per snapshot, so a hash built from Type.id always differs for any re-checked file and the wave never stops — measured at 10 waves and 1,436 of 3,000 files for a body-only edit, versus 1 wave and 1 file with a typeToString hash. It hides in small tests because ids are stable for files that were not re-checked.

nodes.label: getTypeOfSymbol Misses Interface Changes
nodes.rationale: Interfaces report `any` from getTypeOfSymbol and named types print as their own name, so adding a member to an exported interface leaves the naive hash byte-identical. A silent-wrong-answer bug, not a performance issue.

nodes.label: Symbol.getExports Does Not Resolve export *
nodes.rationale: On a 300-statement barrel, Symbol.getExports() returns 1 symbol and Checker.getExportsOfModule() returns 601, because the former is the raw symbol table. Always use the checker.

nodes.label: Batching Is Not Optional
nodes.rationale: The API is IPC, so per-symbol calls each cost a round trip: 9,000 exports take 518 ms unbatched and 31 ms through the array overloads — a 17x difference, and the difference between TS 7 being slower than TS 6 at bulk traversal and being three times faster. Any adapter must be array-first from day one because retrofitting means rewriting the traversal.

nodes.label: Barrel Files Defeat Syntactic Analysis
nodes.rationale: On a barrel of 300 `export * from`, the syntactic view sees 0 named symbols where the checker sees 601, all declared elsewhere. Barrels are the standard package entry point, so this is the common case, not an edge case — and syntax also cannot compute the export-shape hash the incremental algorithm gates on.

nodes.label: Oxc As The Cheap Outer Loop
nodes.rationale: Correct role for Oxc and ast-grep: file discovery, content hashing, a first-cut import graph and syntactic queries that genuinely need no types — never the symbol graph, because their role is strictly syntactic by their own documentation.

nodes.label: Cache-Key Discipline From Nx, Turborepo, Bazel, Rush
nodes.rationale: Adopt the universal content-hash-plus-dependency-cascade pattern and reject the granularity: all four invalidate at task, package or action level because their unit is 'run a command and cache its output', while a symbol graph needs file and symbol granularity. Bazel's action key is the right mental picture — key on (file content hash, project, compiler options, codedocs version, tsgo version).

nodes.label: unstable/sync API Instability Risk
nodes.rationale: The subpath is literally typescript/unstable/sync and 7.1 is promised to be 'new (and different)'; the shipped binary also lags main on method availability. Mitigation: pin the version exactly, probe the server's method set at startup and fail loudly on an untested version. The bet is defensible only because a thin adapter makes it reversible.

nodes.label: No Module Resolution API
nodes.rationale: There is no counterpart to ts.resolveModuleName, so import specifiers must be resolved through checker.getSymbolAtLocation on the specifier and the resulting declaration's NodeHandle.path — 260 ms for 8,100 edges unbatched, so batch it.

nodes.label: Thin, Array-First Adapter
nodes.rationale: The adapter seam is simultaneously the tool-hiding boundary and the batching boundary, so it should expose 'give me facts for these N files' and never 'give me a fact for this symbol' — and stay small enough that a 7.1 rewrite is a week, not a quarter.

nodes.label: Symbol Identity Prior Art
nodes.rationale: Surveys SCIP, LSIF, Stack Graphs, Kythe, Glean and CodeQL from primary sources to answer how symbols should be named and persisted. Verdict: adopt SCIP's naming, reject SCIP as a store, and do not make scip-typescript the sole producer.

nodes.label: SCIP
nodes.rationale: Apache-2.0, versioned, now at the vendor-neutral scip-code org rather than sourcegraph, which materially de-risks depending on it. A single protobuf Index message of Documents, Occurrences and SymbolInformation — a file, not a database.

nodes.label: SCIP Symbol String Grammar
nodes.rationale: Adopt it verbatim as SymbolId rather than inventing a format: it is an open, specified, maintained grammar that already solves fully-qualified cross-package TypeScript naming, and its descriptors encode the Package to File to Symbol ancestry for free. Unlike LSIF's opaque scheme-defined monikers, the grammar itself is specified — the single biggest improvement.

nodes.label: Transmission Format Is Not A Storage Format
nodes.rationale: SCIP and Kythe both say so in their own words, and 'support efficient code navigation by itself' is an explicit SCIP non-goal. Naming and storage are orthogonal layers, and the two mature systems that solved this each adopted a wire format and built their own store.

nodes.label: Version-In-The-ID Is Wrong For A Single-Repo Tool
nodes.rationale: SCIP embeds package version because Sourcegraph indexes many repos at many versions; codedocs indexes one working tree at one commit, where a routine version bump would silently invalidate every symbol in a package and every cross-package reference to it. Normalise it away for workspace packages, keep it for third-party symbols where it carries real information.

nodes.label: local N Ordinals Are Unusable As-Is
nodes.rationale: They are document-scoped (not globally unique) and traversal-ordinal (unstable under any edit inserting an earlier binding). Glean already published half the fix by prefixing the document path; codedocs should do both — prefix the path and flag local symbols non-durable, excluded from documentation anchors and impact baselines.

nodes.label: LSIF
nodes.rationale: A dead end: deprecated and removed by its largest consumer, superseded by SCIP, with no standard symbol grammar and no incrementality provision. Its named failures — a graph of integer ids that produced repo-wide off-by-one navigation bugs, and a wholesale-merge indexer shape resisting parallelism — are why SCIP is shaped as it is.

nodes.label: Stack Graphs
nodes.rationale: Resolves names without naming them — a definition is a node in a file's partial graph and resolution is path-finding — so it cannot supply exportable identifiers. Archived by GitHub in 2025, which under the tool-selection criteria is close to disqualifying.

nodes.label: Per-File Content-Tag Storage Contract
nodes.rationale: Steal stack-graphs' storage model even though its analysis is unusable: SQLite rows keyed by file path holding the serialised per-file analysis plus a content `tag`, skip on tag match, force flag to re-index. It is the only surveyed system with real out-of-the-box file-level incrementality, and the contract is independent of the analysis engine.

nodes.label: Kythe
nodes.rationale: VNames carry path plus a signature with traversal-order ordinals (foo#0), so they break like SCIP and then some. Rejected as Bazel-centric with thin TypeScript support; its (source, kind, target) entry triple is the maximally-general alternative to a typed schema and is worth rejecting for exactly that reason, since it pushes all schema into convention.

nodes.label: Glean
nodes.rationale: The strongest corroboration available: Meta, with the resources to define anything it wants, stores SCIP symbol strings verbatim as a string predicate and patches exactly one defect by prefixing local ids with the document path. Operationally too heavy to consume (Haskell/Hack, server-oriented) for a local-first CLI.

nodes.label: CodeQL Is Licence-Blocked
nodes.rationale: The CLI terms forbid use with any codebase that is not an open-source codebase and forbid database generation in automated analysis or CI, so any dependency on it would make codedocs unusable by its own private-codebase users. Note the trap: the queries are MIT, the CLI is not. Recorded so nobody re-litigates it.

nodes.label: Nobody Has Solved Cross-Commit Symbol Identity
nodes.rationale: All six surveyed systems break identity under rename, move and extract, because stable identity is not derivable from a single snapshot — it requires comparing two, and the comparison is heuristic. This is not an oversight repeated six times: every one of them correctly refused to put a heuristic inside a primary key.

nodes.label: Cross-Commit Continuity As An Inferred Layer
nodes.rationale: 'Is this the same symbol as before?' must be a separate, fallible snapshot-matching question with a confidence attached — git rename detection plus descriptor-suffix matching as a first cut — never a property of SymbolId, which stays deterministic and snapshot-scoped.

nodes.label: scip-typescript Rejected As Producer
nodes.rationale: Keep the format, not the tool: whole-project-only with no changed-files flag, no main-branch commit since 2025-10-03, a documented OOM section for large repos, no library API or type declarations, it bundles its own TypeScript, and SymbolRole has no Call so it cannot distinguish a call from a reference. The live option is codedocs' own extractor over the TypeScript compiler API emitting SCIP-format ids.
